neighbours.label: a resource running out: 'out of', 'low on', 'short of', against abundance on the other side
fire: The clinic is nearly out of vaccine this month.
By Friday the crew had run out of nails.
Our camp is getting low on firewood tonight.
The printer is low on ink again.
The band found itself short of money after the tour.
I'm running short on patience with this landlord.
The bakery sold out of rolls before nine.
The rescue team was almost out of oxygen.
quiet: The clinic has a good supply of vaccine this month.
By Friday the crew had a big box of nails.
Our camp is well stocked with firewood tonight.
The printer is full of ink again.
The band found itself flush with money after the tour.
I'm brimming with patience for this landlord.
The bakery has plenty of rolls before nine.
The rescue team was carrying lots of oxygen.

notes: Probes show it is partly lexical: physical 'ran out of the classroom' and ' out' in 'ran out to' also fire, so the near misses are abundance phrases rather than other senses of 'out'.
